featured_reviews.name: SAHIL RATNAPARKHI
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited FunTime Carnival and overall it was a really great experience. It’s an all-year-round carnival with a good variety of rides, each priced differently — ₹100, ₹200, or ₹300 per person.
The entry ticket is ₹100 per head, and that ticket can be used for any ride of the same cost, which is a nice and flexible system.
We had a great time — bumper cars, kids’ play area, and the zip-line adventure zone were definite highlights. We visited in the second week after opening, so some rides were still being installed and work was ongoing, which is understandable.

One major downside was the Arcade zone inside. It consists of machine games and prize-winning games. Entry is ₹200 per person, and you get three attempts at each of the five games. However, you only get a prize if you win all five games, which is practically impossible since a few games are quite tricky.
The prize is just a small (~30 cm) stuffed toy, which is not worth the price. Bigger toys are displayed but cannot be won. This wasn’t clearly explained beforehand — otherwise, we wouldn’t have played at all. I’d strongly suggest skipping the Arcade section.
Another drawback was the food, which felt way too expensive for what was offered.

Despite these two points, we had a great time overall and would definitely visit again, mainly for the rides and overall carnival vibe.

featured_reviews.name: Mangesh Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
I was recently introduced to The Boardgame Tavern by a friend as a fun weekend activity, and I walked in with absolutely zero knowledge of board games or social deduction games like Blood on the Clocktower. My very first experience at BGT was playing BOTC, and honestly, it was incredible.

Even though I was playing alongside experienced players, the hosts, Suneet and Srushti, made the entire experience feel effortless and welcoming. They explained everything so well that I never felt out of place or overwhelmed. What could have been intimidating turned into a thoroughly enjoyable and engaging session. Since then, I genuinely look forward to attending BOTC games at the Tavern.

The hosts do a fantastic job of creating a fun, inclusive, and comfortable atmosphere for everyone, regardless of experience level. After my first BOTC session, I have gone on to attend several more BOTC games, other social games, and even a Level One D&D session, each of which has been equally enjoyable.

The Boardgame Tavern is truly a special place, and every visit leaves me excited for the next one. I am always looking forward to attending more BGT events and would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a great social gaming experience.

From a shy first timer to now a regular at the Tavern😊, our family is happily thriving and growing with the presence of members like yourself. Truly appreciate your kind words and the love and respect you've shown us ♥️

See you soon Mangesh 👋🏽

featured_reviews.name: Aryaman Patwardhan
featured_reviews.review_text:

We discovered YEY Yaya Kids Club while we were in Bombay for shopping. My wife and I had our little one with us and he was getting bored, so we decided to try this place for about 1.5 hours (₹650) and honestly, it was completely worth every rupee.

The place is very well equipped and thoughtfully designed for kids. Right from the moment you enter, there’s so much for them to explore, trampoline, slides, climbing wall, crazy cars, a kids’ supermarket, kids’ salon, and even that fun bulldozer game where kids pick up balls like mud and slide down. My child didn’t get bored even for a minute.

They also have a big indoor play area, in-house café, and even paid games for extra fun. The space is clean, safe, colourful and very well managed. You can also host birthday parties here which we noticed a lot of parents doing, it’s a perfect setup for that.

What I really liked is that it gives parents a break while kids are happily engaged in a proper play environment. For us, it turned a tiring shopping day into a smooth one because our kid came out smiling and exhausted in the best way 😄

If you’re in Bombay with kids, this place is a life-saver.
Highly recommended. We’ll definitely be coming back. 👍

featured_reviews.name: Gerry Savage
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited on a weekday (Wednesday) but were charged the weekend entry price without any prior notice. It was not a government or national holiday. After being charged, I noticed the bill listed a weekend rate, and when I questioned it, I was told it was because of Pongal (which is not a national holiday). There were no signs, notices, or verbal mention before payment that weekend pricing would apply.
There are excessive restrictions throughout the facility (what children can do, what they can play with, and even how they’re allowed to play). In the pretend play area, costumes are not allowed to be removed from the spot and are only permitted for photos. My child was asked to remove a costume, yet there is no signage explaining this rule. If the area is for photos only, that should be clearly stated.
In the arcade, you only get one play. Several amenities were also not functioning, including the crane game and the rock-climbing area. Other areas were taped up, torn, or visibly run down, making the place feel poorly maintained and potentially unsafe.
There are also rules about where adults are allowed, but no clear indication of which areas are restricted. Overall, the staff managed the space in a very stern manner, which is not appropriate for a children’s play area.
Between the misleading weekday pricing, excessive and unclear rules, broken attractions, and poor maintenance, the experience was extremely disappointing. What was supposed to be a fun outing for my three-year-old turned into a frustrating and unpleasant experience. At best, the practices feel dishonest.
